figures.finding: St Helena levies its own income tax on income earned in St Helena: an individual pays 26% on the first £18,000 of chargeable income and 31% on the rest, after a personal allowance of £7,000 for residents.
figures.applies: Current rates on the government page (2026); the allowance is from the April 2024 guide. Covers St Helena; Ascension and Tristan da Cunha have their own laws, not read.

sources.said: in the case of a person other than a company — 26% on the first £18,000 of such chargeable income; and 31% on the remainder of such chargeable income;
The amount of the Personal Allowance is £7,000 per annum.
From 1st April 2010, St Helena charged income tax only on income earned in St Helena, whether it is earned by a resident or non-resident.

figures.finding: The tax year runs 1 April to 31 March: the self-employed file by 30 June (three months after year end) and pay by 30 September; employees file by 31 July.
figures.applies: Tax year 2026/27. Covers St Helena; Ascension and Tristan da Cunha have their own laws, not read.

Key dates for Employees: 31 JULY – Submission of Tax Return

figures.finding: Employers deduct tax under PAYE using tax codes that include the allowance, with a monthly P6 return within 15 days of each month end.

figures.finding: A non-resident pays St Helena tax on income earned there but gets no personal allowance; a visitor's income is exempt if the visit is no more than 30 days in the tax year, the services are for a non-resident and a non-resident pays.

sources.said: The allowance is available only to residents; non residents will not be entitled to a personal allowance.

income derived in St Helena by a non-resident person (other than a body of persons) during a visit to St Helena, if— (i) the visit does not exceed a total period of 30 days in any tax year; (ii) the services are performed for or on behalf of a non-resident; and (iii) the income is paid by a person who is a non-resident;

figures.finding: There is no VAT; besides income tax St Helena charges a service tax only on insurance and telecommunications services, so a freelancer's fee bears none.
figures.applies: April 2024 guide. Covers St Helena; Ascension and Tristan da Cunha have their own laws, not read.

sources.said: Service Tax - tax will be charged on any insurance service or telecommunications service

figures.finding: St Helena takes no social insurance contribution from pay: its social security benefits (Basic Island Pension, income-related benefits) are charged on the Consolidated Fund, and the Social Security Ordinance levies no contribution.
figures.applies: 2026 on the Ordinance as consolidated on 8 July 2025; an occupational or private pension scheme was not searched for.

sources.said: The benefits provided for in this Ordinance are to be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

figures.finding: The Income Tax Ordinance gives an author's fees or royalties no special treatment: they are income from self-employment, trade or business taxed at the ordinary rates (royalties are property income only for the use of real property), and the exempt-income list has no entry for them.
figures.applies: 2026 on the Ordinance as revised to 1 October 2021.
